content: Between 2007 and 2021, 27 countries conducted national tuberculosis (TB) prevalence surveys. Of these, 22 countries met the epidemiological criteria for conducting a repeat prevalence survey as of April 2022. In these countries, the focus should shift toward maintaining or strengthening national notification and vital registration (VR) systems. As of April 2022, 25 countries had not previously conducted a TB prevalence survey but met the epidemiological criteria for implementing their first survey. For any country meeting these criteria, the feasibility of conducting a survey must also be carefully assessed. According to the WHO guidelines, there are 11 prerequisites for a survey to be feasible. Among the countries meeting the criteria for a first survey, several are likely to face challenges in meeting these feasibility requirements. This is particularly relevant for countries implementing a survey for the first time. The COVID-19 pandemic has likely increased TB prevalence in countries that experienced disruptions in TB case detection, as evidenced by significant reductions in TB case notifications. Countries with major disruptions to TB diagnosis and treatment services during the pandemic may not be able to reliably detect changes in TB prevalence if repeat surveys are conducted within a few years of the pandemic's onset. For future national TB prevalence surveys, two diagnostic algorithms are recommended. The first option involves testing two separate sputum samples from all individuals who screen positive for TB using the Xpert Ultra test, followed by confirmatory testing with liquid culture (MGIT) for those with at least one positive Xpert result. The second option involves liquid culture testing of two separate sputum samples from all screen-positive individuals, complemented by an Xpert Ultra test to provide rapid results for clinical management. Both options allow for the use of other WHO-recommended molecular tests with equivalent or better sensitivity as alternatives to Xpert Ultra. In summary, the implementation of TB prevalence surveys requires careful consideration of epidemiological criteria, feasibility prerequisites, and diagnostic strategies.
